title: Mage Error-Rate Trend Anomaly
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Mage Error-Rate Trend Anomaly' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_mage_error_rate_trend_anomaly` (UC-24.7.66), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Mage Error-Rate Trend Anomaly", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: UC-24.7.66 positive (Mage, Error, Rate, Trend, Anomaly): ingest synthetic events into `index=bi` sourcetype='mage:pipeline' where `avg_rate`, `sd_rate` grouped by `_time` satisfies detection threshold for 'Mage Error-Rate Trend Anomaly'.  Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.

dataSources: Mage pipeline runs (`mage:pipeline`). Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Mage pipeline run events via the Mage API to HEC and scheduler logs via UF. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=mage:pipeline
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as events, sum(eval(status="failed")) as errors by _time
| eval error_rate=round(100*errors/events,2)
| eventstats avg(error_rate) as avg_rate, stdev(error_rate) as sd_rate
| where error_rate>avg_rate+3*sd_rate
| sort - _time
description: Monitors UC-24.7.66 — Mage, Error, Rate, Trend, Anomaly — using `index=bi` sourcetype `mage:pipeline`, grouped by `_time`. Outputs `avg_rate`, `sd_rate` each `1h`; alert when configured threshold. Primary focus: Trend Anomaly. Purpose-built for 'Mage Error-Rate Trend Anomaly' in Operations workflows.
value: Operators running UC-24.7.66 on `mage:pipeline` feeds shorten triage for Trend Anomaly tied to 'Mage Error-Rate Trend Anomaly', lowering operational risk and delayed incident response.
implementation: Ingest Mage logs into index=bi; schedule every 15 minutes over a trailing window and alert on 3-sigma error-rate anomalies.

detailedImplementation:
Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Mage pipeline run events via the Mage API to HEC and scheduler logs via UF. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=mage:pipeline into bi. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_time`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We learn what a normal amount of Mage errors looks like and warn you only when something is genuinely going wrong.
